About Me

Building Digital Growth Through Smart SEO.

I'm Zeeshan Ali, an SEO specialist working with businesses in the USA, UK and worldwide — helping brands get found, cited and recommended, not just in Google's results, but in the AI answers customers now read first.

I handle the full search picture myself: technical audits and fixes, keyword and intent research, on-page optimisation, WordPress SEO, white-hat authority building, and AEO/GEO strategies that put a brand inside AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Gemini responses.

Technical SEO

Technical SEO Audit Project

A full crawl, indexing and Core Web Vitals audit, with prioritised fixes ordered by impact — verified after implementation.

How I handle a technical SEO audit, from start to finish.

The Challenge

Many sites lose rankings not because their content is weak, but because Google cannot crawl, understand, or load their pages properly. Slow pages, broken links, blocked or duplicate pages, and missing schema build up quietly over time, and the site owner usually cannot tell which issue is actually costing rankings. Without a methodical audit, fixes happen at random — the visible problems get attention while the ones holding the site back stay untouched.

What I Do — Step by Step

  1. Crawl the whole site. I run a full crawl of the site, just as a search engine would, and I record every URL, status code, redirect, and error. This gives me the complete picture before I change anything, so no important page is missed and no fix is based on a guess.
  2. Check indexation in Search Console. I check coverage, sitemaps, and which pages Google has actually indexed, and I look for pages blocked by robots rules, noindex tags, or wrong canonical tags. A page that is not indexed cannot rank, so I treat indexation as the first gate every important page must pass.
  3. Test speed and Core Web Vitals. I test loading speed and Core Web Vitals on the pages that matter most, and I note exactly what is slowing each one down — heavy images, unused code, or slow server response. Speed matters because visitors leave slow pages, and search engines notice the same behaviour.
  4. Review structure and internal linking. I review the site structure, URL patterns, and how internal links pass authority from strong pages to the pages that need it. I also find broken links and redirect chains, because a broken path wastes crawl budget and breaks trust for both visitors and search engines.
  5. Audit titles, metas, headings, and images. I audit titles and meta descriptions for length and duplicates, check that headings follow a clear order, and confirm that images carry descriptive alt text. These details tell Google what each page is about, so I fix them page by page instead of applying one template to everything.
  6. Check schema, then prioritise and verify. I check structured data and add or correct schema where it helps Google understand the page, then I turn every finding into a prioritised fix list ordered by impact. I apply the fixes I can, hand over clear instructions for the rest, and re-check in Search Console so every fix is verified rather than assumed done.

What You Get — Deliverables

  • A written technical audit report covering crawl, indexation, speed, structure, and schema.
  • A prioritised fix list, ordered by impact, so the most important problems are fixed first.
  • Hands-on fixes for the issues I can resolve directly, with clear instructions for the rest.
  • Corrected titles, meta descriptions, headings, alt text, and schema where they were missing or duplicated.
  • A re-check in Google Search Console after implementation, confirming what changed.
  • A plain-English monthly progress report, with no jargon and no unverified claims.

How Progress Is Measured

I measure progress in Google Search Console — clicks, impressions, and average position for the site's key pages, together with the number of valid indexed pages and Core Web Vitals results. I compare the figures before the fixes with the figures after, over the same kind of period, and I report only what Search Console itself shows.

The Breakdown

  • Technical health & crawlability — what is blocking Google today.
  • Keyword & intent mapping — what buyers actually search for.
  • Competitor & AI-visibility gaps — where rivals and AI answers win.
  • Content & internal-linking review — what to fix, keep or build next.

Verified Results Only

Progress is reported from Google Search Console — rankings, impressions and clicks you can check yourself. No vanity metrics, no dressed-up screenshots, no traffic numbers that cannot be verified.

You see the work done, the links that went live, and the movement that followed — in plain English, every month.
